title: LightRIM: Light Runtime Integrity Measurement for Linux Kernels in Embedded Applications
problem: Linux kernel security modules provide integrity monitoring but consume substantial computational resources, making them unsuitable for resource-limited embedded systems like autonomous vehicles and robots.
motivation: Linux is widely deployed in embedded domains demanding robust security, but existing integrity measurement approaches incur prohibitive performance overhead; lightweight alternatives preserving coverage are critical.
method: LightRIM performs two-stage hashing on monitored kernel objects and uses event-triggered measurement tied to security value changes. A heuristic algorithm maximizes attack detection rate within CPU budget constraints via randomized measurement intervals to mitigate TOCTOU vulnerabilities.
key_novelty: Event-triggered measurement with heuristic attack-detection-rate optimization under CPU constraints, addressing TOCTOU attacks via randomized interval scheduling.
contributions: Two-stage hashing process reducing monitoring overhead
Event-triggered measurement tied to security value changes
TOCTOU attack mitigation via heuristic CPU-constrained interval randomization achieving extensive attack coverage with <0.7% overhead
limitations: Coverage comparison to full security modules and embedded platform evaluation details not provided.
primary_theme: Lightweight kernel integrity monitoring for embedded systems
